text:
{"body":"## What / why

A "dev environment" = a branch per repo (+ optional redis snapshot), so Kirk
or a friend can spin up a local game stack for a feature/bug-fix with one
command instead of hand-running the checkout dance from
`rpg-project/docs/howto/run-the-game-locally.md` every time.

Adds:
- `scripts/dev-env.sh` — subcommands `up <env>`, `down`, `status`, `pin
  [module...]`, `snapshot save|restore <name>`. Global `--dry-run` (every
  mutating command — checkouts, `go get`, docker/compose, snapshot ops — is
  printed instead of run) and `--root <path>` (workspace root override,
  mainly for testing).
- `envs/dev.env` — first manifest: `rpg-api@dev`, `rpg-dnd5e-web@development`,
  `rpg-toolkit@main`, no snapshot.
- `envs/snapshots/.gitkeep` — snapshots are committed here (small, and it
  makes a bug's exact repro state travel with the branch set that
  reproduces it).
- `docs/dev-environments.md` — friend-facing walkthrough.

## The pseudo-version decision

`rpg-api` consumes local `rpg-toolkit` changes through **pseudo-version pins
in go.mod** (`go get github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/<module>@<pushed-branch>`),
never a `replace` directive pointing at a local checkout. A `replace` would
make the Docker image build and CI depend on a path that only exists on one
machine; a pseudo-version is just a go.mod line that resolves identically
everywhere, so builds and CI stay hermetic. `pin` runs with
`GOPRIVATE=github.com/KirkDiggler/*` so it fetches straight from GitHub
instead of waiting on `proxy.golang.org` to catch up on a fresh push, then
`go mod tidy`.

## Known limitation found while implementing (landmine)

`rpg-api`'s `Dockerfile` build stage runs `go mod download` with no `ARG` for
`GOPROXY`/`GOPRIVATE`/`GOFLAGS` — it's a bare `COPY go.mod go.sum ./` +
`RUN go mod download`. That means `docker build --build-arg GOPRIVATE=...`
would be a no-op (unconsumed build-arg), so `up` does **not** pass one — it
would be misleading dead code. A pin to a just-pushed `rpg-toolkit` commit
can therefore occasionally lag behind `proxy.golang.org` during the image
build even though the `pin` step itself resolved the pushed commit
correctly on the host. Documented in `docs/dev-environments.md` under "Known
limitation"; the real fix is an **`rpg-api` Dockerfile change** (add
`ARG GOPROXY`/`ARG GOPRIVATE` + `ENV` them before `go mod download`) — out of
scope here, tracked as a follow-up to file against `rpg-api`.

## Evidence

**`pin` against a throwaway clone**, network round-trip against the real,
pushed `rpg-toolkit` `main` branch (`--root` pointed at a tmp workspace built
from `git clone` of the real checkouts, never the shared `/home/kirk/game-dev`
checkouts):

```
$ dev-env.sh --root <tmp-root> pin --branch main
==> Pinning 9 module(s) to branch 'main'
    github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core
    ... (9 direct modules parsed from go.mod)
==> go get (GOPRIVATE=github.com/KirkDiggler/*)
go: upgraded github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core v0.10.0 => v0.10.2-0.20260728045433-78f56a786d08
...
==> go mod tidy
==> Resulting pins
    github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core v0.10.2-0.20260728045433-78f56a786d08
    github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter v0.46.3
    ... (all 9 pinned)
```

`go.mod` diff (all 9 direct rpg-toolkit requires moved to pseudo-versions of
the pushed `main`):

```diff
-	github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core v0.10.0
+	github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core v0.10.2-0.20260728045433-78f56a786d08
-	github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter v0.44.1
+	github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter v0.46.3
... (9 lines changed total)
```

Also verified: named short-form modules (`pin encounter rulebooks/dnd5e`),
the branch-does-not-exist-on-origin guard (fails loudly before touching
go.mod), and the ahead-of-origin warning (made an unpushed empty commit on
the throwaway rpg-toolkit clone's `main`, confirmed `pin` warned "1 commit(s)
ahead of origin/main" and still resolved the **pushed** commit, not the
local one).

**`up`/`down`/`status` dry-run**, against a mock multi-repo workspace (real
clones of rpg-api/rpg-toolkit/rpg-dnd5e-web/rpg-deployment, never the shared
checkouts) since even read-only git inspection against the shared checkouts
is outside this session's sandbox:

```
$ dev-env.sh --dry-run --root <mock-root> up dev
==> rpg-toolkit -> main
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-toolkit fetch origin
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-toolkit checkout main
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-toolkit merge --ff-only origin/main
==> rpg-api -> dev
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-api fetch origin
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-api checkout -b dev --track origin/dev
==> rpg-dnd5e-web -> development
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-dnd5e-web fetch origin
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-dnd5e-web checkout -b development --track origin/development
==> Building rpg-api:local from .../rpg-api
    [dry-run] docker build -t rpg-api:local .../rpg-api
==> Starting stack (redis, mongo, 5e-srd-api, envoy, nginx, rpg-api@local)
    [dry-run] docker compose -f .../docker-compose.local-dev.yml -f .../docker-compose.local-api-src.yml up -d
```

Also verified: dirtying one mock repo makes `up` refuse and list exactly
what's dirty, touching nothing; `down --dry-run` prints the matching
`compose down`; `status` against the mock workspace (real, non-dry-run,
since it's read-only) correctly shows per-repo branch/dirty, and — run
against the *real* Docker daemon (containers only, no repo interaction) —
correctly lists the actually-running `rpg-*`/`dnd-*` containers and reports
port 3001 owned by a real `node` process via `ss -ltnp`, confirming the
stale-vite-server trap detection works against live state.

**`snapshot save`/`restore`**, against a throwaway `redis:7-alpine` container
(`dev-env-test-redis` on a non-default port, never `rpg-redis-dev`):
seeded a key, `snapshot save` (real `redis-cli SAVE` + `docker cp`),
overwrote the key plus added a second key, `snapshot restore` without
`--yes` correctly refused (no tty), `snapshot restore --yes` correctly
stopped the container, replaced `dump.rdb`, restarted it, and `redis-cli
KEYS '*'` afterward showed only the original key with its original value —
the extra key and the mutation were both gone. Throwaway container removed
after.

**Static checks:** `bash -n scripts/dev-env.sh` passes. `shellcheck` is not
installed in this environment and was not installed per the task's testing
constraints — flagging in case CI or a reviewer wants to run it.

## Review attention

- The `go mod tidy` step in `pin` runs unconditionally after the `go get`
  loop; if a module's `go get` fails partway through a multi-module pin,
  earlier modules are already pinned in `go.mod` before the script exits —
  no rollback. Acceptable for a dev tool but worth a look.
- `up`'s dirty-check + checkout logic is two passes (validate-all-then-act)

{"body":"## What / why

A "dev environment" = a branch per repo (+ optional redis snapshot), so Kirk
or a friend can spin up a local game stack for a feature/bug-fix with one
command instead of hand-running the checkout dance from
`rpg-project/docs/howto/run-the-game-locally.md` every time.

Adds:
- `scripts/dev-env.sh` — subcommands `up <env>`, `down`, `status`, `pin
  [module...]`, `snapshot save|restore <name>`. Global `--dry-run` (every
  mutating command — checkouts, `go get`, docker/compose, snapshot ops — is
  printed instead of run) and `--root <path>` (workspace root override,
  mainly for testing).
- `envs/dev.env` — first manifest: `rpg-api@dev`, `rpg-dnd5e-web@development`,
  `rpg-toolkit@main`, no snapshot.
- `envs/snapshots/.gitkeep` — snapshots are committed here (small, and it
  makes a bug's exact repro state travel with the branch set that
  reproduces it).
- `docs/dev-environments.md` — friend-facing walkthrough.

## The pseudo-version decision

`rpg-api` consumes local `rpg-toolkit` changes through **pseudo-version pins
in go.mod** (`go get github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/<module>@<pushed-branch>`),
never a `replace` directive pointing at a local checkout. A `replace` would
make the Docker image build and CI depend on a path that only exists on one
machine; a pseudo-version is just a go.mod line that resolves identically
everywhere, so builds and CI stay hermetic. `pin` runs with
`GOPRIVATE=github.com/KirkDiggler/*` so it fetches straight from GitHub
instead of waiting on `proxy.golang.org` to catch up on a fresh push, then
`go mod tidy`.

## Known limitation found while implementing (landmine)

`rpg-api`'s `Dockerfile` build stage runs `go mod download` with no `ARG` for
`GOPROXY`/`GOPRIVATE`/`GOFLAGS` — it's a bare `COPY go.mod go.sum ./` +
`RUN go mod download`. That means `docker build --build-arg GOPRIVATE=...`
would be a no-op (unconsumed build-arg), so `up` does **not** pass one — it
would be misleading dead code. A pin to a just-pushed `rpg-toolkit` commit
can therefore occasionally lag behind `proxy.golang.org` during the image
build even though the `pin` step itself resolved the pushed commit
correctly on the host. Documented in `docs/dev-environments.md` under "Known
limitation"; the real fix is an **`rpg-api` Dockerfile change** (add
`ARG GOPROXY`/`ARG GOPRIVATE` + `ENV` them before `go mod download`) — out of
scope here, tracked as a follow-up to file against `rpg-api`.

## Evidence

**`pin` against a throwaway clone**, network round-trip against the real,
pushed `rpg-toolkit` `main` branch (`--root` pointed at a tmp workspace built
from `git clone` of the real checkouts, never the shared `/home/kirk/game-dev`
checkouts):

```
$ dev-env.sh --root <tmp-root> pin --branch main
==> Pinning 9 module(s) to branch 'main'
    github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core
    ... (9 direct modules parsed from go.mod)
==> go get (GOPRIVATE=github.com/KirkDiggler/*)
go: upgraded github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core v0.10.0 => v0.10.2-0.20260728045433-78f56a786d08
...
==> go mod tidy
==> Resulting pins
    github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core v0.10.2-0.20260728045433-78f56a786d08
    github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter v0.46.3
    ... (all 9 pinned)
```

`go.mod` diff (all 9 direct rpg-toolkit requires moved to pseudo-versions of
the pushed `main`):

```diff
-	github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core v0.10.0
+	github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/core v0.10.2-0.20260728045433-78f56a786d08
-	github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter v0.44.1
+	github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter v0.46.3
... (9 lines changed total)
```

Also verified: named short-form modules (`pin encounter rulebooks/dnd5e`),
the branch-does-not-exist-on-origin guard (fails loudly before touching
go.mod), and the ahead-of-origin warning (made an unpushed empty commit on
the throwaway rpg-toolkit clone's `main`, confirmed `pin` warned "1 commit(s)
ahead of origin/main" and still resolved the **pushed** commit, not the
local one).

**`up`/`down`/`status` dry-run**, against a mock multi-repo workspace (real
clones of rpg-api/rpg-toolkit/rpg-dnd5e-web/rpg-deployment, never the shared
checkouts) since even read-only git inspection against the shared checkouts
is outside this session's sandbox:

```
$ dev-env.sh --dry-run --root <mock-root> up dev
==> rpg-toolkit -> main
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-toolkit fetch origin
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-toolkit checkout main
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-toolkit merge --ff-only origin/main
==> rpg-api -> dev
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-api fetch origin
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-api checkout -b dev --track origin/dev
==> rpg-dnd5e-web -> development
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-dnd5e-web fetch origin
    [dry-run] git -C .../rpg-dnd5e-web checkout -b development --track origin/development
==> Building rpg-api:local from .../rpg-api
    [dry-run] docker build -t rpg-api:local .../rpg-api
==> Starting stack (redis, mongo, 5e-srd-api, envoy, nginx, rpg-api@local)
    [dry-run] docker compose -f .../docker-compose.local-dev.yml -f .../docker-compose.local-api-src.yml up -d
```

Also verified: dirtying one mock repo makes `up` refuse and list exactly
what's dirty, touching nothing; `down --dry-run` prints the matching
`compose down`; `status` against the mock workspace (real, non-dry-run,
since it's read-only) correctly shows per-repo branch/dirty, and — run
against the *real* Docker daemon (containers only, no repo interaction) —
correctly lists the actually-running `rpg-*`/`dnd-*` containers and reports
port 3001 owned by a real `node` process via `ss -ltnp`, confirming the
stale-vite-server trap detection works against live state.

**`snapshot save`/`restore`**, against a throwaway `redis:7-alpine` container
(`dev-env-test-redis` on a non-default port, never `rpg-redis-dev`):
seeded a key, `snapshot save` (real `redis-cli SAVE` + `docker cp`),
overwrote the key plus added a second key, `snapshot restore` without
`--yes` correctly refused (no tty), `snapshot restore --yes` correctly
stopped the container, replaced `dump.rdb`, restarted it, and `redis-cli
KEYS '*'` afterward showed only the original key with its original value —
the extra key and the mutation were both gone. Throwaway container removed
after.

**Static checks:** `bash -n scripts/dev-env.sh` passes. `shellcheck` is not
installed in this environment and was not installed per the task's testing
constraints — flagging in case CI or a reviewer wants to run it.

## Review attention

- The `go mod tidy` step in `pin` runs unconditionally after the `go get`
  loop; if a module's `go get` fails partway through a multi-module pin,
  earlier modules are already pinned in `go.mod` before the script exits —
  no rollback. Acceptable for a dev tool but worth a look.
- `up`'s dirty-check + checkout logic is two passes (validate-all-then-act)
  so a partially-applied checkout across repos shouldn't happen from a dirty
  tree, but a *mid-loop* `git fetch`/`checkout` failure on repo N still
  leaves repos 1..N-1 already switched. Documented via explicit
  `err`+`exit 1` per step, not auto-rolled-back.
- The rpg-api Dockerfile ARG follow-up (GOPROXY/GOPRIVATE build-args) is not
  filed as an rpg-api issue yet — flagging here since it's the actual fix
  for the landmine above.

## Goal / symptom
PI team activity logs and completed issue worktrees accumulate without a bounded retention workflow. On 2026-07-27, `.pi-agents` had grown to 9.4 GiB (individual JSONL files near 1 GiB) and `.pi-worktrees` to 5.8 GiB. Manual conservative cleanup reclaimed about 13.7 GiB, but this should be routine and safe.

## Desired outcome
Provide bounded activity-log rotation/compression and an explicit guarded retirement workflow for PI-owned completed worktrees, with useful disk visibility and no risk to another session's files.

## Contract boundaries
- Streamed external-worker JSONL rotates at a configured byte ceiling; settlement preserves a small readable tail/index and compresses closed chunks.
- Attached RPC activity remains bounded in memory and does not duplicate unbounded transcripts to disk.
- Worktree retirement is allowed only for harness-owned `.pi-worktrees/<repo>-<issue>` paths that are clean, inactive, remote-parity checked, and whose exact HEAD is merged/ancestor of the configured integration target (or otherwise explicitly approved by Kirk).
- Never delete or alter dirty, unmerged, active, unknown, `.claude`, `/tmp/opencode`, primary, or manually owned worktrees. Never infer ownership solely from age.
- Default operation is preview/report; destructive retirement requires explicit confirmation. No daemon or durable task registry.
- GitHub issue/PR/checkpoint remains durable evidence; compressed logs are diagnostics, not task truth.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A synthetic high-volume worker cannot produce an unbounded single activity file.
- [ ] Closed chunks compress automatically and remain inspectable through the viewer.
- [ ] Cleanup preview reports reclaimable bytes and exact refusal reasons.
- [ ] Clean merged harness worktrees can be retired; dirty/unmerged/active/foreign worktrees are discriminating refusals.
- [ ] Integration bases are repository-aware (`development` for web, configured target elsewhere).
- [ ] Full harness/verifier/workspace and disk-boundary tests pass.

## Verification evidence
Fixture tests must cover symlinks, path escape, PID reuse/stale state, remote drift, dirty/untracked files, detached review worktrees, and interrupted compression without timing attacks.

## Related / dependencies
- Managed worker rail/lifecycle: game-dev#37
- Targeted GitHub reads: game-dev#42

{"body":"Observed after the first real QA-walk run of `up dev --clean-web` (2026-07-30).

`--clean-web` does the documented stale-proto fix (`rm -rf node_modules package-lock.json && npm install`), which regenerates `package-lock.json`. The regenerated file differs from the committed one, so rpg-dnd5e-web now has a modified tracked file — and the next `up dev` hard-refuses on exactly that, per the dirty check the script itself enforces. The flag dirties the state its own guard protects.

Options (pick in review):
1. After the reinstall, `git checkout -- package-lock.json` — node_modules is already fixed (the staleness lives in npm's git cache, not the lockfile), so restoring the file doesn't undo the fix.
2. Have the dirty check whitelist package-lock.json when the previous run used --clean-web (stateful, uglier).
3. Just document that --clean-web implies a follow-up lockfile decision (weakest).

Option 1 looks right unless the reinstall legitimately needs to change pinned resolutions, which would be a real dependency change that belongs in a commit anyway.

{"body":"## Summary

Design for the dungeon-builder in-game authoring loop: a dev-gated `PutDungeon`/`ListDungeons` surface plus a `/author` route over real dungeonspec YAML, preserving the edit → save → lobby → play → edit loop.

This update incorporates the settled platform model from rpg-project#175:

- Rooms are stable authored semantic regions; inner walls affect movement/LoS but do not split room identity.
- Dungeon space owns one canonical wall/door edge; the runtime representation is `HexRecord.edges`, not the removed `EncounterService.Space.walls`.
- Room-first and large-area authoring both compile to floor cells, canonical edges, and semantic regions; holes remain obstacle/prop representation until genuine no-floor mechanics exist.
- Target-dialect evolution is not itself a YAML document-version bump; reserve that for an explicit incompatible room/topology change.

The settled sequence is #176 generated geometry truth, #177 authored start, #178 prop facing, #179 authored canonical edges, and #180 cell-authored semantic regions.

`ideas/dungeon-builder/design.md` is the authoritative review artifact. The premature `plan.md` has been removed; a plan is added to this PR only after design approval. This PR remains the tracking surface and must not be merged before that approval.

Design issue: rpg-project#169. References rpg-project#131 and #132.

## Review checks

- [ ] Review the design against rpg-project#175 and #176–#180
- [ ] Confirm the semantic-region/canonical-edge model
- [ ] Approve design before adding any implementation plan or cutting per-repo implementation issues

Design for the dungeon-builder in-game authoring loop: a dev-gated `PutDungeon`/`ListDungeons` surface plus a `/author` route over real dungeonspec YAML, preserving the edit → save → lobby → play → edit loop.

This update incorporates the settled platform model from rpg-project#175:

- Rooms are stable authored semantic regions; inner walls affect movement/LoS but do not split room identity.
- Dungeon space owns one canonical wall/door edge; the runtime representation is `HexRecord.edges`, not the removed `EncounterService.Space.walls`.

{"body":"## Summary

Consolidates the fog-of-war wave into one PR against `main`. This was six stacked PRs (#730 → #732 → #733 → #735 → #736, plus #738 as a sibling of #732); stacking was the process mistake — every fix became another layer instead of landing, and the state became unfollowable. This PR merges all six in stack order into one branch, pins the toolkit to its real published versions, and fixes the one test the toolkit bump breaks.

**Do not close #730/#732/#733/#735/#736/#738 — they stay open for reference until this merges.**

## What each PR contributed

- **#730** — `feat(v2/encounter): consume the fog contract, name the toolkit interface`: viewer-scoped fog of war lands in rpg-api — `ViewerKnowledge`, per-hex `HexKnowledgeChanged`, retires the old whole-room `GeometryRevealed`/entity-appeared broadcast model.
- **#732** — `fix(v2/encounter): restate mover's own hex knowledge live`: the live event stream never told a client a hex stopped being visible (the connect-time snapshot was correct, the live path wasn't) — the mover's own move now restates their full current `KnownHexes` so VISIBLE→REMEMBERED transitions reach the client.
- **#733** — `content: add fog-lab dungeon fixture`: a purpose-built two-room dungeon (4 lit pillars + geometry-fog test surface; one skeleton behind an unlocked door + entity-fog test surface) so fog-of-war playtesting isn't fighting the procedural crypt generator. `RPG_DUNGEON_KEY=fog-lab` selects it — the content-backed key resolution path already existed, no new wiring needed.
- **#735** — `tooling: add local rpg-toolkit/encounter override loop`: lets the Docker dev loop point at a local toolkit checkout without publish → tag → `go get` for every edit-and-look cycle. `scripts/toolkit-local-override.sh` (on/off/status) + `Dockerfile.local-toolkit` + a how-to doc. **The tooling ships; no override is applied in this PR** (see below).
- **#736** — `content: light fog-lab.yaml`: the fixture read as nearly unlit (2 dim candles, zero light in the skeleton room) — added braziers positioned to preserve pillar shadow contrast rather than flattening it.
- **#738** — `fix(v2/encounter): stop reading stale pre-persist state for move knowledge restatement`: #732's restatement raced the orchestrator's persist of the same move — `translateMoveEventWithData` now trusts `MoveEvent.MoverKnownHexes` (the toolkit's own post-move payload, rpg-toolkit#863) directly instead of re-loading from the repo, closing the race entirely. `disclosedEntities` workaround updated to match.

## Toolkit pin

Toolkit is done and tagged — no more overrides, no pseudo-versions:

```
github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter v0.46.3
```

- `v0.46.1` (rpg-toolkit#860) — viewer memory confined to real space (fixes the ~80%-void memory bug)
- `v0.46.2` (rpg-toolkit#861) — a mover is recorded on the one hex they stopped on, not every hex a viewer watched them cross
- `v0.46.3` (rpg-toolkit#863, **pinned**) — `MoveEvent` carries the mover's own post-move knowledge, closing the race #738 fixes on the rpg-api side

`git diff go.mod` shows a real version — no `replace` directive, no `local-toolkit/` directory. Confirmed explicitly (see verification below).

## The #739 fixture fix

`TestProjectFor_HexZoneId_SetViaRegionMembership_NotGeometry` broke on the bump, exactly as expected: it built hexes at negative cube coordinates (`Q=-1`), which convert to an out-of-bounds offset column under `core.Hex.ToPosition()` — `v0.46.1`'s space-membership filter correctly rejects those as not part of the declared `Width`/`Height` grid, so they never reached the wire. This fixture was never testing grid-bounds membership — only `RegionAt`'s own "the door belongs to neither region" behavior (rpg-api#687) — so it moves into non-negative, in-bounds coordinates (verified against the real pointy-top offset conversion, not guessed). Same adjacent triple (chamber1 - door - chamber2, one hex step apart each), same assertions, same "`zone_id` comes from `RegionAt` membership, never geometry" claim — only the absolute position moved. **The toolkit itself is untouched; the assertion is intact.**

## Verification (real output, this session)

- `go build ./...` — clean
- `go vet ./...` — clean
- `gofmt -l internal/` — clean (no output)
- `golangci-lint run ./...` — 29 pre-existing issues, **none** in any file this consolidation touches
- Full unit suite: `go test ./... -count=1` — all packages `ok`
- Real Docker/Redis integration suite (testcontainers, fresh `-count=1`): `internal/integration` (36.5s), `internal/integration/character` (13.5s), `internal/integration/harness` (11.1s) — all `ok`, container spin-up confirmed
- `git diff go.mod`: real version, no replace directive
- `local-toolkit/` directory: does not exist in this tree

## Merge sequence (for the record)

```
origin/main
  + feat/724-hex-knowledge          (#730, fast-forward)
  + feat/remembered-transitions     (#732, fast-forward)
  + feat/fog-lab-dungeon            (#733, fast-forward)
  + feat/toolkit-local-override     (#735, fast-forward)
  + feat/fog-lab-lighting           (#736, fast-forward)
  + fix/move-restatement-stale-read (#738, real merge — this branch descends from #732, not #736)
  + chore: pin encounter@v0.46.3 + fix project_test.go fixture
```

The #738 merge was the one flagged as potentially interesting (it diverges from #732, not #736) — it merged with **zero manual conflicts** via git's `ort` strategy. Verified by inspection, not just absence of conflict markers.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l internal/`, `golangci-lint run ./...`
- [x] Full unit suite + real Docker/Redis integration suite
- [x] Toolkit pinned to a real tag, no replace, no local-toolkit/
- [x] `TestProjectFor_HexZoneId_SetViaRegionMembership_NotGeometry` fixed and passing, assertion intact

References: #730 #732 #733 #735 #736 #738

{"body":"M1 dungeon authoring (rpg-toolkit#846 dungeonspec + rpg-api#710 content store) made authored YAML dungeons real, and prod's default dungeon is now the authored tomb. But the authoring loop today is: edit YAML in `RPG_CONTENT_DIR` → `docker restart rpg-api` → start a fresh encounter. It works and it's blind — you place `[11,3]` in a text file and find out in 3D after a restart. Coordinate traps (odd-q parity, the unplaceable doorRow at height/2, connector columns) are invisible in text and bite every session. With friends the loop is far worse: merge → deploy → restart the Discord activity → rejoin lobby, and there is no separate "prod" — the deployed game IS the dev server running on Kirk's Discord, so any friend-facing authoring must eventually run in that same environment.

This issue tracks a design for an in-game authoring loop: a dev-gated `PutDungeon`/`ListDungeons` surface in rpg-api (runtime dungeon loading, write-through to `RPG_CONTENT_DIR` so the YAML stays the committable artifact) plus a `/author` route in rpg-dnd5e-web — a board/palette/YAML-pane editor that reads and writes the real dungeonspec format, with comment-preserving round-trip, and lets an author go from edit to a lobby with that dungeon preselected and back. The loop itself is the product: play with friends → fail → tweak → replay, with fixes graduating into mechanics, and static maps serving as the design lab for what procedural generation must eventually match.

The design PR (linked below) is the review surface for the full proposal, including phasing (P1 api endpoint alone, P2 lobby dropdown, P3 editor MVP, P4+ schema-driven growth) and testing approach. This design supersedes "M4: in-client tuning panel design" from the M1 dungeon-authoring plan (rpg-project PR #121) — M4 was left as a placeholder ("the in-client tuning panel is its own future design"); this is that design. References #131 (pick-your-dungeon, delivered by P2) and #132 (Dungeon visual fidelity umbrella, adjacent arc).

— asset-pipeline agent, on behalf of KirkDiggler

{"baseRefName":"main","body":"Closes #65

## Summary

- add `scripts/toolkit-override-lab.sh up|down` for a uniquely named API + Envoy lab around the existing API-owned `encounter` override helper
- validate worktrees, Docker network, container names, Envoy/Vite ports, and the approved active module before starting
- build the API automatically with `Dockerfile.local-toolkit`, generate an isolated Envoy upstream, and print the API URL, exact Vite command, and cleanup command
- make cleanup name-scoped and idempotent, including image/config removal plus verification that the API helper reports zero replaces and no `local-toolkit/` residue exists
- reconcile `LOCAL_DEV.md`, `LOCAL_DEV_WORKFLOW.md`, and the fixed-lab Compose guidance: primary is the stable shared baseline; owned fixed labs or this wrapper are the experiment paths
- add a no-live-container regression suite behind `make test`

The wrapper intentionally shares the already-running Redis and D&D API dependencies. It never invokes Compose, so it cannot recreate primary, lab1, or lab2. Tests that create Redis fixtures still own those fixture keys.

## Verification

- `make test` — PASS: happy path, generated Envoy upstream, exact Vite output, container collision, occupied port, cleanup, and repeated cleanup
- `bash -n scripts/toolkit-override-lab.sh scripts/test-toolkit-override-lab.sh` — PASS
- `docker compose -f docker-compose.local-dev.yml -f docker-compose.local-lab.yml config --quiet` — PASS
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — PASS

### Live isolated path

Used detached verification worktrees from current `origin/dev` (API) and `origin/main` (toolkit), leaving the primary checkouts untouched:

- real occupied `:8081` was rejected before the API worktree changed
- `up --name issue65verify --envoy-port 8188 --vite-port 5188` invoked the API helper, host-built the override, Docker-built with `Dockerfile.local-toolkit`, and started only:
  - `rpg-toolkit-lab-issue65verify-api`
  - `rpg-toolkit-lab-issue65verify-envoy`
- `curl http://localhost:8188/` reached the real upstream path and returned Envoy's expected gRPC `415` (`grpc-status: 3`) for a content-type-less request
- `down` succeeded twice; the detached API worktree was clean and no labeled lab container remained
- before/after IDs for the existing services were unchanged: `rpg-api` `ea4fe68b9f35`, `rpg-envoy` `c675b9388ba5`, `rpg-api-lab` `247688b7ab8a`, `rpg-api-lab2` `01377b6779d3`

## Done gate

- **Goal:** yes — there is now one documented reversible command for an unpublished toolkit override through isolated API + Envoy containers.
- **Pattern:** yes — it delegates override mechanics to `rpg-api/scripts/toolkit-local-override.sh` and reuses the canonical Envoy config rather than creating another module mechanism or routing policy.
- **Test:** yes — both deterministic mocked regression coverage and the real Docker/API/Envoy path passed alongside existing services.

- add `scripts/toolkit-override-lab.sh up|down` for a uniquely named API + Envoy lab around the existing API-owned `encounter` override helper
- validate worktrees, Docker network, container names, Envoy/Vite ports, and the approved active module before starting

#!/bin/bash
# toolkit-local-override.sh — iterate on rpg-toolkit/encounter changes in the
# local Docker loop without publish -> version tag -> `go get`.
#
# THE constraint this solves: the local rpg-api image is built with
#   docker build -t rpg-api:local <rpg-api-dir>
# — the build context is the rpg-api directory ALONE. A go.mod `replace`
# pointing outside that directory (e.g. `../../rpg-toolkit/encounter`)
# compiles fine on the host but fails inside Docker, because the toolkit
# source is not in the context. This script instead SYNCS the toolkit
# module's source INTO a gitignored directory inside this repo
# (local-toolkit/encounter) and points the replace at that relative path, so
# it stays inside the build context.
#
# Exactly one module may be overridden: github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter.
# Its sibling-module requires (core, events, tools/spatial, ...) stay at their
# published versions. Do not add another replace: this script rejects any
# unapproved or second active replacement.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/toolkit-local-override.sh on [--src <path-to-rpg-toolkit-checkout>]
#   scripts/toolkit-local-override.sh off
#   scripts/toolkit-local-override.sh status
#
# on:     rsyncs <src>/encounter/ -> local-toolkit/encounter/, then
#         `go mod edit -replace` to point go.mod at it. Re-run `on` after
#         every toolkit edit to re-sync (fast — no publish, no tag, no
#         `go get`); rebuild the image with Dockerfile.local-toolkit
#         afterward (see docs/how-to/local-toolkit-override.md).
# off:    `go mod edit -dropreplace` and deletes local-toolkit/ entirely,
#         restoring go.mod/go.sum to the published pin with no residue.
# status: reports whether the override is currently active.
#
# The `replace` this script adds/removes must NEVER be committed while
# active — it points at a directory (local-toolkit/) that doesn't exist on
# CI or any other machine, and CI's own `go build` would catch an escaped
# replace regardless (defense in depth, not the only line — see
# docs/how-to/local-toolkit-override.md).
set -euo pipefail

MODULE="github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter"
REPO_ROOT="$(git -C "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
LOCAL_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/local-toolkit/encounter"

# replace_modules prints every module path with an active replace directive.
# Keeping this list explicit makes status auditable and lets on/off reject a
# second module rather than silently building a mixed unpublished dependency
# graph.
replace_modules() {
	(cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go mod edit -json | jq -r '.Replace[]? | .Old.Path')
}

assert_only_approved_override() {
	local modules=()
	mapfile -t modules < <(replace_modules)
	if [ "${#modules[@]}" -gt 1 ]; then
		echo "error: exactly one local override is permitted; active modules: ${modules[*]}" >&2
		return 1
	fi
	if [ "${#modules[@]}" -eq 1 ] && [ "${modules[0]}" != "$MODULE" ]; then
		echo "error: unapproved local override for ${modules[0]}; only $MODULE is permitted" >&2
		return 1
	fi
}

usage() {
	echo "Usage: $0 {on [--src <path>]|off|status}" >&2
	exit 1
}

# resolve_src finds an rpg-toolkit checkout to sync from: an explicit --src,
# then TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR, then a couple of common game-dev workspace layouts.
# Errors with a clear message rather than guessing further — silently
# syncing the wrong checkout would be worse than asking.
resolve_src() {
	local explicit="$1"
	local candidates=()
	if [ -n "$explicit" ]; then
		candidates+=("$explicit")
	fi
	if [ -n "${TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR:-}" ]; then
		candidates+=("$TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR")
	fi
	candidates+=(
		"$HOME/game-dev/rpg-toolkit"
		"$REPO_ROOT/../../rpg-toolkit"
		"$REPO_ROOT/../../../rpg-toolkit"
	)
	for c in "${candidates[@]}"; do
		if [ -f "$c/encounter/go.mod" ]; then
			echo "$c"
			return 0
		fi
	done
	echo "error: could not find an rpg-toolkit checkout with encounter/go.mod." >&2
	echo "Pass --src <path>, or set TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR, e.g.:" >&2
	echo "  TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR=/home/kirk/game-dev/rpg-toolkit $0 on" >&2
	return 1
}

cmd_on() {
	local explicit=""
	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
		case "$1" in
		--src)
			explicit="$2"
			shift 2
			;;
		*)
			usage
			;;
		esac
	done

	assert_only_approved_override

	local src
	src="$(resolve_src "$explicit")"

	local module_line
	module_line="$(head -1 "$src/encounter/go.mod")"
	if [ "$module_line" != "module $MODULE" ]; then
		echo "error: $src/encounter/go.mod declares '$module_line', expected 'module $MODULE'" >&2
		exit 1
	fi

	echo "Syncing $src/encounter/ -> $LOCAL_DIR/ ..."
	mkdir -p "$LOCAL_DIR"
	rsync -a --delete --exclude='.git' "$src/encounter/" "$LOCAL_DIR/"

	echo "Pointing go.mod at the local copy ..."
	(cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go mod edit -replace "$MODULE=./local-toolkit/encounter")
	assert_only_approved_override

	echo "Sanity-building on the host ..."
	if ! (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go build ./...); then
		echo "error: host build failed against the synced local copy — check the toolkit edit for compile errors." >&2
		exit 1
	fi

	cat <<EOF

Override ON. go.mod now replaces $MODULE with ./local-toolkit/encounter.

Next steps:
  docker build -f Dockerfile.local-toolkit -t rpg-api:local $REPO_ROOT
  (cd /home/kirk/game-dev/rpg-deployment && \\
   docker compose -f docker-compose.local-dev.yml \\
                  -f docker-compose.local-api-src.yml \\
                  up -d rpg-api)

Re-run '$0 on' after every toolkit edit to re-sync.
Run '$0 off' when done — publish the toolkit change, bump the version tag,
then remove the override (never leave it active on a branch you push).
EOF
}

cmd_off() {
	assert_only_approved_override

	echo "Dropping the replace directive ..."
	(cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go mod edit -dropreplace "$MODULE")

	echo "Removing $LOCAL_DIR ..."
	rm -rf "$REPO_ROOT/local-toolkit"

	echo "Sanity-building against the published module ..."
	if ! (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go build ./...); then
		echo "error: build failed after removing the override — go.mod/go.sum may need attention (git diff go.mod go.sum)." >&2
		exit 1
	fi

	echo "Override OFF. go.mod/go.sum are back on the published pin, local-toolkit/ removed."
}

cmd_status() {
	local modules=()
	mapfile -t modules < <(replace_modules)
	if [ "${#modules[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
		echo "Active replace modules (0): none"
		echo "Override OFF: $MODULE resolves to its published version."
	else
		echo "Active replace modules (${#modules[@]}): ${modules[*]}"
		if ! assert_only_approved_override; then
			return 1
		fi
		local replace
		replace="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go list -m -f '{{if .Replace}}{{.Replace.Path}} => {{.Replace.Dir}}{{end}}' "$MODULE" 2>/dev/null || true)"
		if [ -z "$replace" ]; then
			echo "error: approved module is listed but has no resolvable replacement" >&2
			return 1
		fi
		echo "Override ON: $MODULE => $replace"
	fi
	if [ -d "$LOCAL_DIR" ]; then
		echo "local-toolkit/encounter/ exists on disk ($(find "$LOCAL_DIR" -name '*.go' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') .go files)."
	else
		echo "local-toolkit/encounter/ does not exist."
	fi
}

case "${1:-}" in
on)
	shift
	cmd_on "$@"
	;;
off)
	cmd_off
	;;
status)
	cmd_status
	;;
*)
	usage
	;;
esac

	mapfile -t modules < <(replace_modules)
	if [ "${#modules[@]}" -gt 1 ]; then
		echo "error: exactly one local override is permitted; active modules: ${modules[*]}" >&2
		return 1
	fi
	if [ "${#modules[@]}" -eq 1 ] && [ "${modules[0]}" != "$MODULE" ]; then
		echo "error: unapproved local override for ${modules[0]}; only $MODULE is permitted" >&2
		return 1
	fi
}

usage() {
	echo "Usage: $0 {on [--src <path>]|off|status}" >&2
	exit 1
}

# resolve_src finds an rpg-toolkit checkout to sync from: an explicit --src,
# then TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR, then a couple of common game-dev workspace layouts.
# Errors with a clear message rather than guessing further — silently
# syncing the wrong checkout would be worse than asking.
resolve_src() {
	local explicit="$1"
	local candidates=()
	if [ -n "$explicit" ]; then
		candidates+=("$explicit")
	fi
	if [ -n "${TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR:-}" ]; then
		candidates+=("$TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR")
	fi
	candidates+=(
		"$HOME/game-dev/rpg-toolkit"
		"$REPO_ROOT/../../rpg-toolkit"
		"$REPO_ROOT/../../../rpg-toolkit"
	)
	for c in "${candidates[@]}"; do
		if [ -f "$c/encounter/go.mod" ]; then
			echo "$c"
			return 0
		fi
	done
	echo "error: could not find an rpg-toolkit checkout with encounter/go.mod." >&2
	echo "Pass --src <path>, or set TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR, e.g.:" >&2
	echo "  TOOLKIT_SRC_DIR=/home/kirk/game-dev/rpg-toolkit $0 on" >&2
	return 1
}

cmd_on() {
	local explicit=""
	while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
		case "$1" in
		--src)
			explicit="$2"
			shift 2
			;;
		*)
			usage
			;;
		esac
	done

	assert_only_approved_override

	local src
	src="$(resolve_src "$explicit")"

	local module_line
	module_line="$(head -1 "$src/encounter/go.mod")"
	if [ "$module_line" != "module $MODULE" ]; then
		echo "error: $src/encounter/go.mod declares '$module_line', expected 'module $MODULE'" >&2
		exit 1
	fi

	echo "Syncing $src/encounter/ -> $LOCAL_DIR/ ..."
	mkdir -p "$LOCAL_DIR"
	rsync -a --delete --exclude='.git' "$src/encounter/" "$LOCAL_DIR/"

	echo "Pointing go.mod at the local copy ..."
	(cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go mod edit -replace "$MODULE=./local-toolkit/encounter")
	assert_only_approved_override

	echo "Sanity-building on the host ..."
	if ! (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go build ./...); then
		echo "error: host build failed against the synced local copy — check the toolkit edit for compile errors." >&2
		exit 1
	fi

	cat <<EOF

Override ON. go.mod now replaces $MODULE with ./local-toolkit/encounter.

Next steps:
  docker build -f Dockerfile.local-toolkit -t rpg-api:local $REPO_ROOT
  (cd /home/kirk/game-dev/rpg-deployment && \\
   docker compose -f docker-compose.local-dev.yml \\
                  -f docker-compose.local-api-src.yml \\
                  up -d rpg-api)

Re-run '$0 on' after every toolkit edit to re-sync.
Run '$0 off' when done — publish the toolkit change, bump the version tag,
then remove the override (never leave it active on a branch you push).
EOF
}

cmd_off() {
	assert_only_approved_override

	echo "Dropping the replace directive ..."
	(cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go mod edit -dropreplace "$MODULE")

	echo "Removing $LOCAL_DIR ..."
	rm -rf "$REPO_ROOT/local-toolkit"

	echo "Sanity-building against the published module ..."
	if ! (cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go build ./...); then
		echo "error: build failed after removing the override — go.mod/go.sum may need attention (git diff go.mod go.sum)." >&2
		exit 1
	fi

	echo "Override OFF. go.mod/go.sum are back on the published pin, local-toolkit/ removed."
}

cmd_status() {
	local modules=()
	mapfile -t modules < <(replace_modules)
	if [ "${#modules[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
		echo "Active replace modules (0): none"
		echo "Override OFF: $MODULE resolves to its published version."
	else
		echo "Active replace modules (${#modules[@]}): ${modules[*]}"
		if ! assert_only_approved_override; then
			return 1
		fi
		local replace
		replace="$(cd "$REPO_ROOT" && go list -m -f '{{if .Replace}}{{.Replace.Path}} => {{.Replace.Dir}}{{end}}' "$MODULE" 2>/dev/null || true)"

			echo "error: approved module is listed but has no resolvable replacement" >&2
			return 1
		fi
		echo "Override ON: $MODULE => $replace"
	fi
	if [ -d "$LOCAL_DIR" ]; then
		echo "local-toolkit/encounter/ exists on disk ($(find "$LOCAL_DIR" -name '*.go' | wc -l | tr -d ' ') .go files)."
	else
		echo "local-toolkit/encounter/ does not exist."
	fi
}

case "${1:-}" in
on)
	shift
	cmd_on "$@"
	;;
off)
	cmd_off
	;;
status)
	cmd_status
	;;
*)
	usage
	;;
esac

# dev-env.sh — named dev environments for the rpg game stack: a branch per
# repo (+ optional redis snapshot) so one command spins up a local stack
# pinned to a known-good set of branches for a feature or bug-fix.
#
# See docs/dev-environments.md for the full walkthrough.
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/dev-env.sh [--dry-run] [--root <path>] <command> [args...]
#
# Commands:
#   up <env> [--restore] [--clean-web]
#       Read envs/<env>.env; for each repo with a *_BRANCH set, refuse if it
#       has staged or modified TRACKED changes (untracked files — stray
#       .mcp.json, .claude/worktrees/, one-off symlinks — are normal and just
#       noted, not blocking; git itself refuses a checkout that would
#       overwrite an untracked path, which remains the backstop), else fetch
#       + checkout that branch. Then build the rpg-api image and start the
#       stack (redis, mongo, 5e-srd-api, envoy, nginx; rpg-api via the
#       local-api-src overlay). --restore restores the manifest's SNAPSHOT
#       (if any). --clean-web nukes and reinstalls rpg-dnd5e-web's
#       node_modules (the stale-proto fix).
#
#   down
#       Stop the stack (compose down). Never touches repo checkouts.
#
#   status
#       Per repo: branch + dirty/clean. Running rpg/dnd containers.
#       Who owns ports 3001/3002/3003/8080 (stale vite servers from another
#       checkout squatting :3001 is a known trap).
#
#   pin [module...] [--branch <b>]
#       In the rpg-api checkout, pin github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/*
#       modules to pseudo-versions of a pushed rpg-toolkit branch, then
#       `go mod tidy`. Default modules: every direct rpg-toolkit require in
#       rpg-api/go.mod. Named modules are short forms (encounter,
#       rulebooks/dnd5e). Branch defaults to the local rpg-toolkit checkout's
#       current branch — verified to exist on origin, with a loud warning if
#       local HEAD is ahead of it (the pin resolves the PUSHED commit).
#
#   snapshot save <name>
#       SAVE the redis container's dataset and copy it to
#       envs/snapshots/<name>.rdb.
#
#   snapshot restore <name> [--yes]
#       Destructive: replace the redis container's dataset with
#       envs/snapshots/<name>.rdb. Requires --yes or an interactive y/N.
#
# Global flags:
#   --dry-run       print every mutating command instead of running it
#                   (checkouts, go get, docker, compose, snapshot ops)
#   --root <path>   workspace root override (default: this script's ../)

set -uo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Output helpers (match bootstrap.sh's style)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log()  { printf '\n\033[1;36m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
ok()   { printf '    \033[1;32m\xe2\x9c\x93\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
skip() { printf '    \033[2m- %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
warn() { printf '    \033[1;33m!\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
err()  { printf '    \033[1;31m\xe2\x9c\x97\033[0m %s\n' "$1" >&2; }

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dev-env.sh [--dry-run] [--root <path>] <command> [args...]

Commands:
  up <env> [--restore] [--clean-web]   bring the stack up on envs/<env>.env
  down                                  stop the stack (containers only)
  status                                repo branches/dirty, containers, ports
  pin [module...] [--branch <b>]        pin rpg-toolkit pseudo-versions
  snapshot save <name>                  save redis state to envs/snapshots/
  snapshot restore <name> [--yes]       restore redis state (destructive)

Global flags:
  --dry-run       print mutating commands instead of running them
  --root <path>   workspace root override (default: script-dir/..)

See docs/dev-environments.md for the full walkthrough.
EOF
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Global flag parsing — --dry-run/--root may appear anywhere before the
# command or its arguments.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
DRY_RUN=0
ROOT_OVERRIDE=""
ARGS=()
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1; shift ;;
    --root) ROOT_OVERRIDE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --root=*) ROOT_OVERRIDE="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) ARGS+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

if [ -n "$ROOT_OVERRIDE" ]; then
  ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT_OVERRIDE" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || { err "--root: no such directory: $ROOT_OVERRIDE"; exit 1; }
else

  printf '%s_BRANCH' "$upper"

COMPOSE_API_SRC_REL="rpg-deployment/docker-compose.local-api-src.yml"

  while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
    case "$1" in

      --clean-web) clean_web_flag=1; shift ;;

  set -a

  set +a

  # a *_BRANCH set has staged or modified TRACKED changes. Untracked files

  # checkout) don't block this; they're only noted, since git itself already

  # the real backstop. ---
  local -a targets=()
  local -a dirty_report=()
  local -a untracked_notes=()
  local repo var branch repo_path tracked_dirty untracked
  for repo in $(workspace_repos); do
    var="$(env_var_for_repo "$repo")"
    branch="${!var:-}"
    [ -n "$branch" ] || continue

    repo_path="$ROOT/$repo"
    if [ ! -d "$repo_path/.git" ]; then
      err "$repo: not a git checkout at $repo_path"
      exit 1
    fi

    targets+=("$repo:$branch")

    tracked_dirty="$(git -C "$repo_path" status --porcelain -uno)"
    if [ -n "$tracked_dirty" ]; then
      dirty_report+=("$repo ($repo_path):")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bootstrap.sh — set up (or re-sync) Kirk's D&D-game asset-pipeline dev
# environment on this machine. Idempotent: detects what's already present
# and only installs/copies what's missing. Safe to re-run any time — that's
# also how this repo doubles as a sync mechanism (pull latest, re-run,
# converge).
#
# Usage: ./bootstrap.sh   (run from anywhere; it resolves its own location)

set -uo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Resolve the workspace root as this script's own directory. No hardcoded
#    /home/kirk paths — this must work wherever the repo got cloned.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
# shellcheck source=scripts/workspace-repos.sh
source "$ROOT/scripts/workspace-repos.sh"

log()  { printf '\n\033[1;36m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
ok()   { printf '    \033[1;32m✓\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
skip() { printf '    \033[2m- %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
warn() { printf '    \033[1;33m!\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }

NEXT_STEPS=()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. nvm + node v24
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Checking nvm + node v24"

export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
if [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ]; then
  ok "nvm already installed ($NVM_DIR)"
else
  warn "nvm not found — installing"
  curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.1/install.sh | bash
  ok "nvm installed"
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
\. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

if nvm ls 24 >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -d "$NVM_DIR/versions/node" ] && ls "$NVM_DIR/versions/node" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^v24\.'; then
  ok "node v24 already installed ($(ls "$NVM_DIR/versions/node" | grep '^v24\.' | tail -1))"
else
  warn "node v24 not found via nvm — installing"
  nvm install 24
  ok "node v24 installed"
fi
nvm use 24 >/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Blender
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Checking Blender"

if command -v blender >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "blender already installed ($(command -v blender))"
else
  warn "blender not found"
  if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "installing via apt-get (needs sudo)"
    sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y blender
    ok "blender installed"
  else
    warn "no apt-get available — install Blender manually, then re-run"
    NEXT_STEPS+=("Install Blender manually (headless FBX->GLB conversion needs it), then re-run ./bootstrap.sh")
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Clone the workspace repositories into the workspace root, if absent.
#    Never clobber an existing clone — optionally fetch to freshen refs.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Checking game repos"

for repo in $(workspace_repos); do
  if [ -d "$ROOT/$repo/.git" ]; then
    ok "$repo already cloned — fetching"
    git -C "$ROOT/$repo" fetch --quiet || warn "$repo: fetch failed (check SSH auth)"
  else

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bootstrap.sh — set up (or re-sync) Kirk's D&D-game asset-pipeline dev
# environment on this machine. Idempotent: detects what's already present
# and only installs/copies what's missing. Safe to re-run any time — that's
# also how this repo doubles as a sync mechanism (pull latest, re-run,
# converge).
#
# Usage: ./bootstrap.sh   (run from anywhere; it resolves its own location)

set -uo pipefail

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. Resolve the workspace root as this script's own directory. No hardcoded
#    /home/kirk paths — this must work wherever the repo got cloned.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"
# shellcheck source=scripts/workspace-repos.sh
source "$ROOT/scripts/workspace-repos.sh"

log()  { printf '\n\033[1;36m==>\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
ok()   { printf '    \033[1;32m✓\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }
skip() { printf '    \033[2m- %s\033[0m\n' "$1"; }
warn() { printf '    \033[1;33m!\033[0m %s\n' "$1"; }

NEXT_STEPS=()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. nvm + node v24
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Checking nvm + node v24"

export NVM_DIR="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
if [ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ]; then
  ok "nvm already installed ($NVM_DIR)"
else
  warn "nvm not found — installing"
  curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.1/install.sh | bash
  ok "nvm installed"
fi

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
\. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

if nvm ls 24 >/dev/null 2>&1 && [ -d "$NVM_DIR/versions/node" ] && ls "$NVM_DIR/versions/node" 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^v24\.'; then
  ok "node v24 already installed ($(ls "$NVM_DIR/versions/node" | grep '^v24\.' | tail -1))"
else
  warn "node v24 not found via nvm — installing"
  nvm install 24
  ok "node v24 installed"
fi
nvm use 24 >/dev/null

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Blender
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
log "Checking Blender"

if command -v blender >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ok "blender already installed ($(command -v blender))"
else
  warn "blender not found"
  if command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "installing via apt-get (needs sudo)"
    sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y blender
    ok "blender installed"
  else
    warn "no apt-get available — install Blender manually, then re-run"
    NEXT_STEPS+=("Install Blender manually (headless FBX->GLB conversion needs it), then re-run ./bootstrap.sh")
  fi
fi

for repo in $(workspace_repos); do

    else

done

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

log "Installing npm dependencies"

if [ -f "$ROOT/tools/browser/package.json" ]; then

else

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# restart-dev-env.sh — recreate the standing rpg-dnd5e-web `development`
# branch dev server after a merge into that branch (rpg-project#153's
# development-branch trial). Pulls the standing worktree to the branch's
# latest, re-syncs assets, and restarts vite on a dedicated port so the
# environment always serves what's currently on `development` — never the
# primary local-dev loop's :3001.
#
# Standing worktree: rpg-dnd5e-web/.worktrees/development-env, tracking
# origin/development. Not created by this script — see rpg-project#153 for
# the one-time setup (git worktree add .worktrees/development-env
# development, then npm install once).
#
# Usage: ./scripts/restart-dev-env.sh
#   (run after every merge into rpg-dnd5e-web's `development` branch)

set -euo pipefail

WEB_DEV_ENV="$HOME/game-dev/rpg-dnd5e-web/.worktrees/development-env"
PORT=3011
LOG_FILE="/tmp/vite-dev-env.log"

if [ ! -d "$WEB_DEV_ENV" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: standing dev-env worktree not found at $WEB_DEV_ENV" >&2
  echo "One-time setup: cd rpg-dnd5e-web && git worktree add .worktrees/development-env development" >&2
  exit 1
fi

cd "$WEB_DEV_ENV"

echo "==> Pulling development branch (fast-forward only)"
git pull --ff-only

echo "==> Syncing assets"
npm run assets:sync

echo "==> Freeing port $PORT if a previous dev server is still listening"
# Kill only the LISTEN owner on this exact port -- never pkill -f, which can
# self-match this script's own process line or any other vite instance on
# the machine (see game-dev's local-dev-loop notes on the stale-vite trap).
PIDS="$(lsof -ti :"$PORT" -sTCP:LISTEN || true)"
if [ -n "$PIDS" ]; then
  echo "    killing PID(s): $PIDS"
  kill $PIDS
else
  echo "    nothing listening on $PORT"
fi

echo "==> Starting vite on :$PORT (background, logging to $LOG_FILE)"
nohup npm run dev -- --port "$PORT" > "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1 &
disown

echo "==> Done. Dev env serving development@$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) at http://localhost:$PORT"
echo "    Log: $LOG_FILE"

# Dockerfile.local-toolkit — dev-only variant of Dockerfile for use with
# scripts/toolkit-local-override.sh's local-toolkit/encounter override (see
# docs/how-to/local-toolkit-override.md). Never used by production compose
# files or CI; only scripts/toolkit-local-override.sh's own instructions
# reference it.
#
# The ONLY difference from Dockerfile: `COPY . .` runs BEFORE `go mod
# download` instead of after. That reordering is load-bearing when a
# `replace` in go.mod points at a filesystem path INSIDE this build context
# (local-toolkit/encounter/) — `go mod download` needs that directory to
# already exist to resolve the replaced module's own dependency graph, and
# the original Dockerfile's go.mod/go.sum-only COPY (a layer-caching
# optimization for the normal, no-replace case) doesn't bring it in until
# the LATER `COPY . .`, which is too late. This file trades that caching
# optimization away — acceptable here since a local-toolkit edit means a
# full rebuild is wanted anyway — for correctness under an active replace.
#
# Harmless without an active override: with no `replace` in go.mod, this
# produces the exact same image as Dockerfile, just without the go.mod/
# go.sum layer-cache split.
FROM golang:1.25-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Install build dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache git

# Copy the full source (including any local-toolkit/ override) FIRST — see
# this file's header for why the ordering differs from Dockerfile.
COPY . .
RUN go mod download

# Build the application
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux go build -installsuffix cgo -o server ./cmd/server

# Final stage
FROM alpine:3.20

# Install ca-certificates for HTTPS requests
RUN apk --no-cache add ca-certificates

# Create a non-root user and group
RUN adduser -D -g '' appuser

# Set the working directory
WORKDIR /home/appuser

# Copy the binary from builder stage and adjust ownership
COPY --from=builder /app/server .
RUN chown appuser:appuser /home/appuser/server

# Switch to the non-root user
USER appuser

# Expose the gRPC port
EXPOSE 50051

# Run the server
CMD ["./server", "server"]

---
name: local rpg-toolkit override loop
description: Iterate on rpg-toolkit/encounter changes in the local Docker loop without publish -> tag -> go get
updated: 2026-07-27
---

# How to iterate on rpg-toolkit changes without publishing

The normal toolkit dependency loop (see [update-proto-dependency.md](update-proto-dependency.md)'s
"Update toolkit dependency" section) is: edit rpg-toolkit, commit, tag a new
module version, `go get` it into rpg-api. That's the right process for a
change you're confident in — but a bug that needs several edit-and-look
cycles (e.g. rpg-toolkit#858, #859) makes a publish-per-attempt loop
impractical.

This script lets you point rpg-api's build at a **local** rpg-toolkit
checkout instead, for `github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter` only.
It rejects any unapproved replacement or second replacement; one local module
is the entire override budget for an iteration.

## The constraint this solves

The local rpg-api container is built with:

```bash
docker build -t rpg-api:local <rpg-api-dir>
```

The build context is the rpg-api directory **alone**. A `go.mod` `replace`
pointing outside it (e.g. `../../rpg-toolkit/encounter`) compiles fine with
a plain `go build` on the host, then **fails inside Docker**, because the

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run an unpublished rpg-toolkit/encounter checkout through an isolated API + Envoy lab.
set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
MODULE="github.com/KirkDiggler/rpg-toolkit/encounter"
ACTION="${1:-}"
[ $# -gt 0 ] && shift || true
API_DIR=""
TOOLKIT_DIR=""
LAB_NAME=""
ENVOY_PORT=""
VITE_PORT=""
NETWORK="rpg-deployment_rpg-network"

usage() {
  cat >&2 <<'EOF'
Usage:
  scripts/toolkit-override-lab.sh up --api <rpg-api-worktree> --toolkit <rpg-toolkit-worktree> \
      --name <unique-name> --envoy-port <port> [--vite-port <port>] [--network <docker-network>]
  scripts/toolkit-override-lab.sh down --api <rpg-api-worktree> --name <unique-name>
EOF
  exit 2
}

die() { echo "error: $*" >&2; exit 1; }

while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --api) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage; API_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --toolkit) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage; TOOLKIT_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --name) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage; LAB_NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --envoy-port) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage; ENVOY_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --vite-port) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage; VITE_PORT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    --network) [ $# -ge 2 ] || usage; NETWORK="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    *) usage ;;
  esac
done

[ "$ACTION" = up ] || [ "$ACTION" = down ] || usage
[ -n "$API_DIR" ] && [ -n "$LAB_NAME" ] || usage
[[ "$LAB_NAME" =~ ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$ ]] || die "lab name must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}"
API_DIR="$(cd "$API_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || die "API worktree does not exist: $API_DIR"
OVERRIDE="$API_DIR/scripts/toolkit-local-override.sh"
[ -x "$OVERRIDE" ] || die "missing executable override helper: $OVERRIDE"
API_CONTAINER="rpg-toolkit-lab-${LAB_NAME}-api"
ENVOY_CONTAINER="rpg-toolkit-lab-${LAB_NAME}-envoy"
IMAGE="rpg-api:toolkit-lab-${LAB_NAME}"
STATE_DIR="$ROOT/tmp/toolkit-labs/$LAB_NAME"

container_exists() { docker container inspect "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
image_exists() { docker image inspect "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

verify_clean() {
  local failed=0 clean_status=""
  if ! clean_status="$("$OVERRIDE" status)"; then
    echo "error: API override helper status check failed after cleanup" >&2
    failed=1
  elif ! grep -Fq "Active replace modules (0): none" <<<"$clean_status"; then
    echo "error: API override helper still reports an active replace after cleanup" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  if grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*replace[[:space:]]+$MODULE[[:space:]]*=>[[:space:]]*\./local-toolkit/encounter" "$API_DIR/go.mod"; then
    echo "error: override residue remains in $API_DIR/go.mod; run '$OVERRIDE off' and inspect the worktree" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  if [ -e "$API_DIR/local-toolkit" ]; then
    echo "error: override residue remains at $API_DIR/local-toolkit" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  return "$failed"
}

remove_lab_resources() {
  local failed=0
  for container in "$ENVOY_CONTAINER" "$API_CONTAINER"; do
    for _ in 1 2 3; do
      container_exists "$container" || break
      docker rm -f "$container" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      for _ in 1 2 3 4 5; do
        container_exists "$container" || break 2
        sleep 0.2
      done
    done
    if container_exists "$container"; then
      echo "error: failed to remove name-scoped container '$container'" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  done
  for _ in 1 2 3; do
    image_exists "$IMAGE" || break
    docker image rm "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sleep 0.2
  done
  if image_exists "$IMAGE"; then
    echo "error: failed to remove name-scoped image '$IMAGE'" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
  if [ -e "$STATE_DIR" ]; then
    echo "error: failed to remove generated lab state '$STATE_DIR'" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  return "$failed"
}

cleanup() {
  local failed=0
  if ! remove_lab_resources; then failed=1; fi
  if ! "$OVERRIDE" off; then
    echo "error: API override helper cleanup failed" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  if ! verify_clean; then failed=1; fi
  if [ "$failed" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "error: lab '$LAB_NAME' cleanup is incomplete; inspect the errors above" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "Lab '$LAB_NAME' is down; containers, image, generated Envoy config, and API override residue removed."
}

if [ "$ACTION" = down ]; then
  cleanup
  exit 0
fi

[ -n "$TOOLKIT_DIR" ] && [ -n "$ENVOY_PORT" ] || usage
TOOLKIT_DIR="$(cd "$TOOLKIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || die "toolkit worktree does not exist: $TOOLKIT_DIR"
[ -f "$TOOLKIT_DIR/encounter/go.mod" ] || die "toolkit checkout lacks encounter/go.mod: $TOOLKIT_DIR"
[ -f "$API_DIR/Dockerfile.local-toolkit" ] || die "API worktree lacks Dockerfile.local-toolkit"

docker network inspect "$NETWORK" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "Docker network '$NETWORK' does not exist; start the local dependency stack first"
for container in "$API_CONTAINER" "$ENVOY_CONTAINER"; do
  container_exists "$container" && die "container '$container' already exists; choose another --name or run this lab's down command"
done

validate_port() {
  local label="$1" port="$2"
  [[ "$port" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$port" -ge 1024 ] && [ "$port" -le 65535 ] || die "$label must be an integer from 1024 to 65535"
  python3 - "$port" <<'PY' || die "$label $port is already in use; choose another port"
import socket, sys
port = int(sys.argv[1])
sockets = []
for family, address in ((socket.AF_INET, "0.0.0.0"), (socket.AF_INET6, "::")):
    try:
        sock = socket.socket(family, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 0)
        if family == socket.AF_INET6:
            sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_IPV6, socket.IPV6_V6ONLY, 1)
        sock.bind((address, port))
        sockets.append(sock)
    except OSError:
        sys.exit(1)
PY
}
validate_port "Envoy port" "$ENVOY_PORT"
if [ -n "$VITE_PORT" ]; then
  [ "$VITE_PORT" != "$ENVOY_PORT" ] || die "Vite port must differ from Envoy port"
  validate_port "Vite port" "$VITE_PORT"
fi

initial_status=""
if ! initial_status="$("$OVERRIDE" status)"; then
  die "API override helper status failed before startup; inspect the API worktree"
fi
override_preexisting=false
if grep -Fq "Override ON: $MODULE" <<<"$initial_status"; then
  override_preexisting=true
elif ! grep -Fq "Active replace modules (0): none" <<<"$initial_status"; then
  die "API override state is neither clean nor the approved encounter override"
fi

mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
sed "s/address: rpg-api  # Docker service name/address: $API_CONTAINER  # isolated toolkit lab/" \
  "$ROOT/envoy/envoy.yaml" > "$STATE_DIR/envoy.yaml"
grep -q "address: $API_CONTAINER" "$STATE_DIR/envoy.yaml" || die "failed to generate isolated Envoy upstream"

PREEXISTING_BACKUP="$STATE_DIR/preexisting-api-override"
if [ "$override_preexisting" = true ]; then
  mkdir -p "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP"
  cp -a "$API_DIR/go.mod" "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.mod"
  if [ -e "$API_DIR/go.sum" ]; then cp -a "$API_DIR/go.sum" "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.sum"; fi
  [ -e "$API_DIR/local-toolkit" ] || die "approved pre-existing override has no local-toolkit directory to preserve"
  cp -a "$API_DIR/local-toolkit" "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/local-toolkit"
fi

up_failed() {
  local status=$? rollback_failed=0 restored_status=""
  if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
    if [ "$override_preexisting" = true ]; then
      cp -a "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.mod" "$API_DIR/go.mod" || rollback_failed=1
      if [ -e "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.sum" ]; then
        cp -a "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.sum" "$API_DIR/go.sum" || rollback_failed=1
      else
        rm -f "$API_DIR/go.sum" || rollback_failed=1
      fi
      rm -rf "$API_DIR/local-toolkit"
      cp -a "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/local-toolkit" "$API_DIR/local-toolkit" || rollback_failed=1
      if ! restored_status="$("$OVERRIDE" status)" || ! grep -Fq "Override ON: $MODULE" <<<"$restored_status"; then
        echo "error: failed to restore the pre-existing approved API override" >&2
        rollback_failed=1
      fi
    else
      if ! "$OVERRIDE" off; then
        echo "error: API helper failed while rolling back a partial override activation" >&2
        rollback_failed=1
      fi
      if ! verify_clean; then rollback_failed=1; fi
    fi
    if ! remove_lab_resources; then rollback_failed=1; fi
    if [ "$rollback_failed" -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "error: lab startup failed and rollback is incomplete; inspect the errors above" >&2
    elif [ "$override_preexisting" = true ]; then
      echo "error: lab startup failed; isolated resources were removed and the pre-existing API override was restored" >&2
    else
      echo "error: lab startup failed; isolated resources and partial API override state were removed" >&2
    fi
  fi
  exit "$status"
}
trap up_failed EXIT

"$OVERRIDE" on --src "$TOOLKIT_DIR"
status_output="$("$OVERRIDE" status)"
grep -Fq "Override ON: $MODULE" <<<"$status_output" || die "existing override helper did not activate the approved encounter module"

docker build -f "$API_DIR/Dockerfile.local-toolkit" -t "$IMAGE" "$API_DIR"
docker run -d --name "$API_CONTAINER" --network "$NETWORK" \
  --label "rpg.toolkit-lab=$LAB_NAME" \
  -e PORT=50051 -e LOG_LEVEL=info -e REDIS_ADDR=redis:6379 -e AUTH_DEV_MODE=true \
  -e DND5E_API_URL=http://dnd-api:3000/api/2014/ "$IMAGE" >/dev/null
docker run -d --name "$ENVOY_CONTAINER" --network "$NETWORK" \
  --label "rpg.toolkit-lab=$LAB_NAME" -p "$ENVOY_PORT:8080" \
  -v "$STATE_DIR/envoy.yaml:/etc/envoy/envoy.yaml:ro" envoyproxy/envoy:v1.31-latest \
  /usr/local/bin/envoy -c /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml -l info >/dev/null

for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$API_CONTAINER")" = true ] || die "API container exited; inspect with: docker logs $API_CONTAINER"
  [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$ENVOY_CONTAINER")" = true ] || die "Envoy container exited; inspect with: docker logs $ENVOY_CONTAINER"
  if curl -sS -o /dev/null "http://localhost:$ENVOY_PORT/"; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
curl -sS -o /dev/null "http://localhost:$ENVOY_PORT/" || die "Envoy did not become reachable on port $ENVOY_PORT"

trap - EXIT
cat <<EOF
Lab '$LAB_NAME' is ready.
API URL: http://localhost:$ENVOY_PORT
Vite command:
  VITE_API_HOST=http://localhost:$ENVOY_PORT npm run dev${VITE_PORT:+ -- --port $VITE_PORT}
Cleanup:
  $ROOT/scripts/toolkit-override-lab.sh down --api $API_DIR --name $LAB_NAME

Re-run 'up' after toolkit edits (run 'down' first). This lab shares the existing local Redis/D&D dependencies but does not recreate primary, lab1, or lab2.
EOF

    failed=1
  elif ! grep -Fq "Active replace modules (0): none" <<<"$clean_status"; then
    echo "error: API override helper still reports an active replace after cleanup" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  if grep -Eq "^[[:space:]]*replace[[:space:]]+$MODULE[[:space:]]*=>[[:space:]]*\./local-toolkit/encounter" "$API_DIR/go.mod"; then
    echo "error: override residue remains in $API_DIR/go.mod; run '$OVERRIDE off' and inspect the worktree" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  if [ -e "$API_DIR/local-toolkit" ]; then
    echo "error: override residue remains at $API_DIR/local-toolkit" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  return "$failed"
}

remove_lab_resources() {
  local failed=0
  for container in "$ENVOY_CONTAINER" "$API_CONTAINER"; do
    for _ in 1 2 3; do
      container_exists "$container" || break
      docker rm -f "$container" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
      for _ in 1 2 3 4 5; do
        container_exists "$container" || break 2
        sleep 0.2
      done
    done
    if container_exists "$container"; then
      echo "error: failed to remove name-scoped container '$container'" >&2
      failed=1
    fi
  done
  for _ in 1 2 3; do
    image_exists "$IMAGE" || break
    docker image rm "$IMAGE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    sleep 0.2
  done
  if image_exists "$IMAGE"; then
    echo "error: failed to remove name-scoped image '$IMAGE'" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
  if [ -e "$STATE_DIR" ]; then
    echo "error: failed to remove generated lab state '$STATE_DIR'" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  return "$failed"
}

cleanup() {
  local failed=0
  if ! remove_lab_resources; then failed=1; fi
  if ! "$OVERRIDE" off; then
    echo "error: API override helper cleanup failed" >&2
    failed=1
  fi
  if ! verify_clean; then failed=1; fi
  if [ "$failed" -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "error: lab '$LAB_NAME' cleanup is incomplete; inspect the errors above" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  echo "Lab '$LAB_NAME' is down; containers, image, generated Envoy config, and API override residue removed."
}

if [ "$ACTION" = down ]; then
  cleanup
  exit 0
fi

[ -n "$TOOLKIT_DIR" ] && [ -n "$ENVOY_PORT" ] || usage
TOOLKIT_DIR="$(cd "$TOOLKIT_DIR" 2>/dev/null && pwd)" || die "toolkit worktree does not exist: $TOOLKIT_DIR"
[ -f "$TOOLKIT_DIR/encounter/go.mod" ] || die "toolkit checkout lacks encounter/go.mod: $TOOLKIT_DIR"
[ -f "$API_DIR/Dockerfile.local-toolkit" ] || die "API worktree lacks Dockerfile.local-toolkit"

docker network inspect "$NETWORK" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "Docker network '$NETWORK' does not exist; start the local dependency stack first"
for container in "$API_CONTAINER" "$ENVOY_CONTAINER"; do
  container_exists "$container" && die "container '$container' already exists; choose another --name or run this lab's down command"
done

validate_port() {
  local label="$1" port="$2"
  [[ "$port" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$port" -ge 1024 ] && [ "$port" -le 65535 ] || die "$label must be an integer from 1024 to 65535"
  python3 - "$port" <<'PY' || die "$label $port is already in use; choose another port"
import socket, sys
port = int(sys.argv[1])
sockets = []
for family, address in ((socket.AF_INET, "0.0.0.0"), (socket.AF_INET6, "::")):
    try:
        sock = socket.socket(family, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        sock.setsockopt(socket.SOL_SOCKET, socket.SO_REUSEADDR, 0)
        if family == socket.AF_INET6:
            sock.setsockopt(socket.IPPROTO_IPV6, socket.IPV6_V6ONLY, 1)
        sock.bind((address, port))
        sockets.append(sock)
    except OSError:
        sys.exit(1)
PY
}
validate_port "Envoy port" "$ENVOY_PORT"
if [ -n "$VITE_PORT" ]; then
  [ "$VITE_PORT" != "$ENVOY_PORT" ] || die "Vite port must differ from Envoy port"
  validate_port "Vite port" "$VITE_PORT"
fi

initial_status=""
if ! initial_status="$("$OVERRIDE" status)"; then
  die "API override helper status failed before startup; inspect the API worktree"
fi
override_preexisting=false
if grep -Fq "Override ON: $MODULE" <<<"$initial_status"; then
  override_preexisting=true
elif ! grep -Fq "Active replace modules (0): none" <<<"$initial_status"; then
  die "API override state is neither clean nor the approved encounter override"
fi

mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR"
sed "s/address: rpg-api  # Docker service name/address: $API_CONTAINER  # isolated toolkit lab/" \
  "$ROOT/envoy/envoy.yaml" > "$STATE_DIR/envoy.yaml"
grep -q "address: $API_CONTAINER" "$STATE_DIR/envoy.yaml" || die "failed to generate isolated Envoy upstream"

PREEXISTING_BACKUP="$STATE_DIR/preexisting-api-override"
if [ "$override_preexisting" = true ]; then
  mkdir -p "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP"
  cp -a "$API_DIR/go.mod" "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.mod"
  if [ -e "$API_DIR/go.sum" ]; then cp -a "$API_DIR/go.sum" "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.sum"; fi
  [ -e "$API_DIR/local-toolkit" ] || die "approved pre-existing override has no local-toolkit directory to preserve"
  cp -a "$API_DIR/local-toolkit" "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/local-toolkit"
fi

up_failed() {
  local status=$? rollback_failed=0 restored_status=""
  if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
    if [ "$override_preexisting" = true ]; then
      cp -a "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.mod" "$API_DIR/go.mod" || rollback_failed=1
      if [ -e "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.sum" ]; then
        cp -a "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/go.sum" "$API_DIR/go.sum" || rollback_failed=1
      else
        rm -f "$API_DIR/go.sum" || rollback_failed=1
      fi
      rm -rf "$API_DIR/local-toolkit"
      cp -a "$PREEXISTING_BACKUP/local-toolkit" "$API_DIR/local-toolkit" || rollback_failed=1
      if ! restored_status="$("$OVERRIDE" status)" || ! grep -Fq "Override ON: $MODULE" <<<"$restored_status"; then
        echo "error: failed to restore the pre-existing approved API override" >&2
        rollback_failed=1
      fi
    else
      if ! "$OVERRIDE" off; then
        echo "error: API helper failed while rolling back a partial override activation" >&2
        rollback_failed=1
      fi
      if ! verify_clean; then rollback_failed=1; fi
    fi
    if ! remove_lab_resources; then rollback_failed=1; fi
    if [ "$rollback_failed" -ne 0 ]; then
      echo "error: lab startup failed and rollback is incomplete; inspect the errors above" >&2
    elif [ "$override_preexisting" = true ]; then
      echo "error: lab startup failed; isolated resources were removed and the pre-existing API override was restored" >&2
    else
      echo "error: lab startup failed; isolated resources and partial API override state were removed" >&2
    fi
  fi
  exit "$status"
}
trap up_failed EXIT

"$OVERRIDE" on --src "$TOOLKIT_DIR"
status_output="$("$OVERRIDE" status)"
grep -Fq "Override ON: $MODULE" <<<"$status_output" || die "existing override helper did not activate the approved encounter module"

docker build -f "$API_DIR/Dockerfile.local-toolkit" -t "$IMAGE" "$API_DIR"
docker run -d --name "$API_CONTAINER" --network "$NETWORK" \
  --label "rpg.toolkit-lab=$LAB_NAME" \
  -e PORT=50051 -e LOG_LEVEL=info -e REDIS_ADDR=redis:6379 -e AUTH_DEV_MODE=true \
  -e DND5E_API_URL=http://dnd-api:3000/api/2014/ "$IMAGE" >/dev/null
docker run -d --name "$ENVOY_CONTAINER" --network "$NETWORK" \
  --label "rpg.toolkit-lab=$LAB_NAME" -p "$ENVOY_PORT:8080" \
  -v "$STATE_DIR/envoy.yaml:/etc/envoy/envoy.yaml:ro" envoyproxy/envoy:v1.31-latest \
  /usr/local/bin/envoy -c /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml -l info >/dev/null

for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$API_CONTAINER")" = true ] || die "API container exited; inspect with: docker logs $API_CONTAINER"
  [ "$(docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' "$ENVOY_CONTAINER")" = true ] || die "Envoy container exited; inspect with: docker logs $ENVOY_CONTAINER"
  if curl -sS -o /dev/null "http://localhost:$ENVOY_PORT/"; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done
curl -sS -o /dev/null "http://localhost:$ENVOY_PORT/" || die "Envoy did not become reachable on port $ENVOY_PORT"

trap - EXIT
cat <<EOF
Lab '$LAB_NAME' is ready.
API URL: http://localhost:$ENVOY_PORT
Vite command:
  VITE_API_HOST=http://localhost:$ENVOY_PORT npm run dev${VITE_PORT:+ -- --port $VITE_PORT}
Cleanup:
  $ROOT/scripts/toolkit-override-lab.sh down --api $API_DIR --name $LAB_NAME

Re-run 'up' after toolkit edits (run 'down' first). This lab shares the existing local Redis/D&D dependencies but does not recreate primary, lab1, or lab2.
EOF
